newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast lt. crudes fall after ANS discounted.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast lt. crudes fall after ANS discounted.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes saw a flurry of activity early Friday, after traders reported Exxon sold two cargoes of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, the region's benchmark, at sharply lower discounts.
Traders said Exxon sold around 400,000 barrels of ANS to Shell's Anacortes, Wash., refinery for June delivery at $1.48 a barrel under June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing crude.
Neither company could be reached to confirm the deal, which was done late Thursday. Exxon and Shell normally refuse to confirm oil sales.
And Tosco confirmed they bought 400,000 barrels of ANS at $1.50 early Friday.
"It's all a function of price," said a trader, when asked why Tosco chose ANS. Exxon sold the cargo, the trader said, but declined to say which Tosco plant would run the crude.
The minus $1.50 deal represents a 18-cent-a-barrel fall from May 5, when ANS sold for $1.32 under June WTI.
Meanwhile, the wider discounts caused outright ANS prices to slip 13 cents a barrel early Friday to $18.80-19.00.
High volumes of imports have weakened demand from West Coast refiners, with Chevron seen taking in Arab light and medium crudes for June, traders said.

Chevron and Tosco's heavy reliance on foreigns for June has also cut demand for lighter California San Joaquin Valley (SJV) grades. Those refiners, along with Ultramar, normally buy SJV as a component of Line 63, a ANS lookalike.
"We have not bought a drop," said one trader, referring to SJV light, which has left U.S. government marketers unable to sell 5,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of Elk Hills light crude in June and July.
Ultramar is rumored to be shopping for Oriente.
Traders said Atlantic Richfield Co. was close to buying two 400,000 barrel cargoes of Mesa crude, a Venezuelan lookalike to Alaska North Slope (gravity 30 degrees), for June delivery.
Another major buyer, Texaco, was well supplied for June after taking two to three cargoes of Oriente, traders said.
Kern River crude was unchanged early Friday at $14.01/14.11 a barrel.
Wilmington and Line 63 markets remained idle.
